html:
The Trans-Caspian Railway was built by the Russian army from the eastern shore of the Caspian Sea into Central Asia, starting in 1879. It roughly follows the old Silk Road.

Its first purpose was war. Russian troops needed supplies to fight the Turkmen, and after the siege of Geok Tepe in 1881 the line pushed on under General Mikhail Annenkov. It reached Ashgabat, then Merv in 1886, Samarkand in 1888 and Tashkent in 1898.

The railway tied the new Russian rule in Central Asia to the rest of the empire. It also brought settlers and carried cotton north, which turned large areas of the oases over to cotton for Russian mills. The British watched its advance toward Afghanistan with alarm, as part of the Great Game.
